# Presentation Abstracts

Guidance for crafting conference abstracts that grab a program committee's attention.

## When to Use

- Writing a new presentation abstract from scratch
- Refining an existing abstract for resubmission
- Reviewing an abstract before submission
- Helping structure the core message of a talk

## Start Here

**First, ask the user:**

> "Are you targeting a specific conference? If so, I can research past talks and abstracts to help tailor your submission. Would you like me to do that first?"

If yes, run the **conference-research** skill first, then come back with those insights.

## Core Idea

Every abstract needs **one startling sentence** — a specific, bold, falsifiable claim that makes a
reviewer want to know how you can say that. Everything else supports it.

The four-sentence structure: **problem → why it matters → startling sentence → implication.**
